newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end stable at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: German shares end stable at higher levels.

text.p: German share trade lost momentum in afternoon electronic dealings on Thursday and ended the day shy of record highs, but dealers again expressed amazement at the market's resilience.

The IBIS DAX index, which measures electronic trade in German shares, ended at 3,272.58 points, up 27.56 points. At one point in afternoon trade the index came within two points of its lifetime high of 3,286.37 points.
"This market is crazy, but let the cash roll in and just enjoy the ride," said one trader. "Most traders have discounted a correction already -- indeed they are hoping for it."
The dollar was one of the main factors behind the strength of the market. While slightly weaker against the mark at 1.68, it was still strong enough to underpin German share trade.
The DAX index, which measures floor trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended up 38.85 points, or 1.20 percent, at 3,276.72 points, not far off a lifetime high of 3,287.79 points.
Among the main winners in afternoon trade was haircare product maker Wella AG, which ended up 5.12 percent at 904 marks after technical signals and dollar strength helped to boost the stock.

Also in favour was steel group Thyssen AG, which ended up over five percent at 3,64.20 marks. Dealers said everyone was "jumping on the bandwagon", as market players sought to look for stocks which had been neglected in the bull run.
Sectoral rotation favoured builders Philipp Holzmann AG and Hochtief AG. Holzmann ended up 4.24 percent at 492 marks, while Hochtief rose 1.50 marks to 73.20 marks later on.

Karstadt AG continued to enjoy favour over the day after Germany's Wirtschaftwoche magazine said on Wednesday that major shareholders in the retailer wanted to replace Karstadt chief executive Walter Deuss.

Traders noted Karstadt advanced despite expectations for the retailer to post a 1996 loss of nearly 300 million marks and plans to close more stores. Shares ended the day up 3.17 percent at 554 marks.
Chemicals and pharmaceutical giant Bayer AG also ended the day higher, up 1.56 marks at 71.28 marks, boosted by news that it planned to increase its research and development spending.
Bayer said it had "a good dozen" products under development that would add over 10 billion marks in new sales.

Shares in truck manufacturer MAN AG ended down 7.50 marks to 433.50 marks after the group said it was aiming in its 1996/97 business year to earn a profit about equal to year-earlier results despite a drop in first-half profit.
MAN said group net profit for the last six months of 1996 had fallen to 80 million marks from 110 million marks.
